title: Capacity hedge sprint: pocket budgeting & pricing sensitivity proposal
content:
Purpose:

This is a working proposal for a compact "pocket" budget that sits alongside the FY27 baseline. Goal: create 3 small, prioritized reserve buckets that can be deployed during short token-price shocks or demand surges without moving the baseline hiring plan or opening a full reforecast. The doc includes: quick headcount swap options, pricing-sensitivity triggers, a 12‑week runway sprint funding approach, and recommended playbook steps for Finance + EngOps.

Context / why now:
- Model-hosting spot and reserved GPU prices have shown high variability in 2026; two short but sharp price spikes occurred in Q2 and Q3.
- Hosted API usage velocity has become more concentrated among a handful of customers; burst capacity exposure is asymmetric.
- We want a low-friction way to fund temporary capacity/burst without committing long-term FTEs or breaking SLA commitments for Dedicated customers.

Design principles:
1) Small and fast: pockets are sized to cover 8–12 weeks of observed burst demand, not replace long-term capacity planning.
2) Fungible: funds can be used for burst reserved capacity, short-term contractor labor, or temporary cross-region routing costs.
3) Trigger-driven: explicit triggers (pricing or utilization) automatically nominate a pocket for release; Finance approval path is short (owner + VP).

Pockets (proposed three buckets):
- Pocket A (Safety: Pricing Shock) — $1.2M ceiling; covers a 25% sustained token cost increase across hosted model mix for 8 weeks.
- Pocket B (Surge Capacity) — $900k ceiling; used to spin up short-term Dedicated burst nodes or purchase cloud reserved capacity contracts for 12 weeks.
- Pocket C (People Flex) — $600k ceiling; short-term contractors/temps for SRE/infra blitzes or solutions engineering to stabilize high-value customer incidents.

Sizing rationale (quick math):
- Baseline monthly token spend (hosted API): $3.1M. A 25% shock for two months ≈ $1.55M additional. We cap Pocket A at $1.2M (assumes mitigations e.g., throttling and routing policy recover ~20% of exposure).
- Dedicated burst pool costs (GPU hours + network): observed historical 12-week peak used to derive $900k.
- People flex: average contractor fully loaded rate $20k/month; 8 concurrent contractors for 3 months ≈ $480k -> rounded to $600k to include hiring overhead/eng ramp.

Headcount swap options (shortlist, for product/eng hiring committee):
- Swap option 1: Delay 2 mid-level infra hires (Q1-FY27) -> frees ~ $360k in FY27 spend; convert to Pocket C if triggers fire.
- Swap option 2: Convert 4 headcount offers to contractor slots through Q3 -> frees $520k in headcount budget but increases short-term run rate when used.
- Swap option 3: Use vesting acceleration window closeout savings (~$150k) + small credit line to bridge smaller shocks.

Pricing sensitivity scenarios (hosted API token mix):
Scenario table (illustrative):

| Scenario | Token price delta | Token mix change | Additional FY27 spend (6 months) | Pocket recommended |
|---------:|-----------------:|----------------:|---------------------------------:|-------------------|
| Base     | 0%               | current mix     | $0                                | none              |
| Mild     | +10%             | same            | $1.0M                             | Pocket A partial  |
| Moderate | +20%             | 5% shift to large models | $1.9M                    | Pocket A + B      |
| Severe   | +35%             | 10% shift to large models| $3.6M                   | Escalate to board |
Assumptions: token price = blended cost across model catalog; consumption elasticity during shock = -0.05 (i.e., small demand reduction unless throttled).

Operational triggers (proposed):
- Financial trigger: 7-day trailing token cost > 18% of monthly baseline OR 14-day run rate that implies > 15% MoM increase = nominate Pocket A.
- Utilization trigger: 5-minute tail latency or throughput reduction observed on >=2 regions for >6 hours = nominate Pocket B.
- Customer-impact trigger: any P0 incident affecting >1 enterprise account where Dedicated fallback is insufficient = nominate Pocket C.

Playbook & approvals:
1) Auto-notify: EngOps & Finance receive an automated Slack and PagerDuty message (channel #capacity-hedge).
2) Quick review: owner (Finance ops lead) + EngOps lead evaluate P&L impact; if matches trigger, release pocket with VP sign-off within 24 hours.
3) Usage tracking: all pockets must be tracked against the master pocket sheet (linked artifact) and reconciled weekly.
4) Replenishment rules: pockets are replenished only at quarter boundaries and only if baseline run-rate supports it.

Quick sheet (excerpts) — conservative burn projection for Pocket A under Moderate scenario:

| Week | Additional token $ | Cumulative burn | Remaining pocket |
|-----:|------------------:|-----------------:|-----------------|
| 1    | 110,000           | 110,000         | 1,090,000        |
| 2    | 120,000           | 230,000         | 970,000          |
| 3    | 150,000           | 380,000         | 820,000          |
| 4    | 180,000           | 560,000         | 640,000          |
| 5    | 170,000           | 730,000         | 470,000          |
| 6    | 180,000           | 910,000         | 290,000          |
| 7    | 140,000           | 1,050,000       | 150,000          |
| 8    | 120,000           | 1,170,000       | 30,000           |
Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: pockets delay necessary long-term hiring -> mitigation: pockets require a 1:1 review with hiring committee if used for >2 months continuously.
- Risk: pockets are exhausted during a protracted shock -> mitigation: staged throttling rules and early customer communication templates.
- Risk: moral hazard (teams rely on pockets) -> mitigation: include usage quotas per product area and de-prioritization of non-critical feature work during pocket usage.

Recommended next steps (short timeline):
- Nov 12: Finance + EngOps tabletop exercise simulating 20% token-price shock (owner: Jordan). -> create detailed runbook play actions.
- Nov 18: Legal review of contractor conversion and any procurement implications (owner: Priya).
- Nov 24: Present pocket proposal to CFO and Head of Product for provisional approval.
- Dec 1: Finalize pocket governance doc and wire into billing/console incident hooks.

Open questions / To do list:
- How to reflect pocket accounting in CAC & LTV metrics (tracking is easy; attributing cost is ambiguous).
- Decide whether Dedicated enterprise credits should be eligible (some customers already have reserved credits).
- Confirm maximum cumulative pocket exposure across FY27 (do we cap at $2.5M total active at a time?).

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally conservative on the people-cost side to preserve runway.
- The pockets are a hedge, not a substitute for proper capacity planning or pricing adjustments.
- If approved, we'll publish a shorter one-page runbook for on-call and a tiny dashboard widget in Console.

Slack refs: <#eng-ops>, <#finance-ops>. Jira: FIN-482 (pocket governance epic).

-- Jordan
